```typescript
import type { Clue, JourneyStop, RootStage, Roots, WordEntry, WordPart } from '../types';
import { MAX_GUESSES, formatAttested } from './puzzle';

const MASK_DOT = '·';

/** Letters only, lowercase, accents stripped — for comparing forms against the answer. */
function letters(text: string): string {
  return text
    .normalize('NFD')
    .replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g, '')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z]/g, '');
}

function sameText(a: string, b: string): boolean {
  return letters(a) === letters(b);
}

/** Keeps a form's leading `*`/`-`, first letter and trailing `-`: "back" → "b···", "-ful" → "-f··". */
export function maskForm(form: string): string {
  const match = form.match(/^([*-]*)(.)(.*?)(-*)$/u);
  if (!match) return form;
  const [, lead, first, rest, trail] = match;
  return lead + first + MASK_DOT.repeat([...rest].length) + trail;
}

/** Masks whole-word occurrences of the answer inside clue text. */
export function redact(text: string, answer: string): string {
  const escaped = answer.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
  return text.replace(new RegExp(`\\b${escaped}\\b`, 'gi'), (match) => maskForm(match));
}

/** A form gives the answer away if it contains it, or is the answer minus a letter or two. */
function formLeaks(form: string, answer: string): boolean {
  const f = letters(form);
  const a = letters(answer);
  if (!f) return false;
  return f.includes(a) || (a.includes(f) && f.length >= a.length - 2);
}

/** Transparent compounds (back + fire) spell the answer, so their forms are masked. */
function guardParts(parts: WordPart[], answer: string): WordPart[] {
  const a = letters(answer);
  const spellsAnswer = parts.map((p) => letters(p.form)).join('') === a;
  return parts.map((part) => {
    const f = letters(part.form);
    const hide = spellsAnswer || (f.length >= 4 && a.includes(f));
    return {
      ...part,
      form: hide ? maskForm(part.form) : part.form,
      gloss: part.gloss && redact(part.gloss, answer),
    };
  });
}

function journeyClue(roots: Roots): Clue {
  const stops: JourneyStop[] = [];
  const add = (lang: string, uncertain?: boolean) => {
    const last = stops.at(-1);
    if (last?.lang === lang) last.uncertain = last.uncertain && uncertain;
    else stops.push({ lang, uncertain });
  };
  // "from Latin caro + levare": the parts' language comes before the first recorded form.
  const partsLang = roots.parts[0]?.lang;
  if (partsLang && partsLang !== roots.lineage[0]?.lang) add(partsLang);
  roots.lineage.forEach((stage) => add(stage.lang, stage.uncertain));
  add('English');
  return { kind: 'journey', stops };
}

function attestedClue(attested: string | null): Clue {
  return {
    kind: 'text',
    text: attested
      ? `First recorded in English ${formatAttested(attested).phrase}.`
      : 'No firm early date survives in the record.',
  };
}

/** Clue 3: what the parts or the oldest ancestor meant — never the forms themselves. */
function meaningClue(entry: WordEntry, roots: Roots): { clue: Clue; shown?: string } {
  const answer = entry.word;
  const { parts, lineage } = roots;
  if (parts.length >= 2 && parts.every((p) => p.gloss)) {
    return { clue: { kind: 'parts', parts: guardParts(parts, answer), showForms: false } };
  }
  const stage = lineage.find((s) => s.gloss && !sameText(s.gloss, entry.clues[0]));
  if (stage?.gloss) {
    return {
      clue: { kind: 'meaning', lang: stage.lang, gloss: redact(stage.gloss, answer), uncertain: stage.uncertain },
      shown: stage.gloss,
    };
  }
  return { clue: { kind: 'text', text: redact(entry.clues[2], answer) }, shown: entry.clues[2] };
}

/** Clue 5 (near-giveaway): the actual root forms. */
function rootClue(entry: WordEntry, roots: Roots, shown: string[]): Clue {
  const answer = entry.word;
  const { parts, lineage } = roots;
  if (parts.length >= 2) return { kind: 'parts', parts: guardParts(parts, answer), showForms: true };

  const withForm = lineage.filter((s): s is RootStage & { form: string } => Boolean(s.form));
  const newest = withForm.at(-1);
  if (!newest) return { kind: 'text', text: redact(entry.clues[3], answer) };

  const glossFor = (stage: RootStage) =>
    stage.gloss && !shown.some((t) => sameText(t, stage.gloss!)) ? redact(stage.gloss, answer) : undefined;
  const sameSpelling = letters(newest.form) === letters(answer);
  const masked = { lang: newest.lang, form: maskForm(newest.form), gloss: glossFor(newest), sameSpelling, uncertain: newest.uncertain };

  // Borrowed unchanged, with a meaning to go on: "Same spelling in Spanish: b·····, 'district, suburb'".
  if (sameSpelling && newest.gloss) return { kind: 'source', ...masked };

  const safe = [...withForm].reverse().find((s) => !formLeaks(s.form, answer));
  if (safe) {
    return { kind: 'source', lang: safe.lang, form: safe.form, gloss: glossFor(safe), sameSpelling: false, uncertain: safe.uncertain };
  }
  return { kind: 'source', ...masked };
}

/**
 * Five clues, hardest to easiest: the route into English, first recorded date,
 * what its roots meant, its earliest English sense, then the root forms themselves.
 */
export function getClues(entry: WordEntry): Clue[] {
  const { roots } = entry;
  if (!roots) {
    return entry.clues.slice(0, MAX_GUESSES).map((text) => ({ kind: 'text', text: redact(text, entry.word) }));
  }
  const earliestSense = entry.clues[0];
  const meaning = meaningClue(entry, roots);
  const shown = [earliestSense, ...(meaning.shown ? [meaning.shown] : [])];
  return [
    journeyClue(roots),
    attestedClue(roots.attested),
    meaning.clue,
    { kind: 'text', text: redact(earliestSense, entry.word) },
    rootClue(entry, roots, shown),
  ];
}
```

```typescript
import type { JourneyStop } from '../types';
import { ChevronIcon } from './icons';
import { LanguageName } from './LanguageName';

const CHIP = 'inline-flex items-center rounded-[20px] px-2.5 py-1 text-[13px] leading-none';

export function JourneyTrail({ stops }: { stops: JourneyStop[] }) {
  const nativeOnly = stops.length === 1;

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <span>{nativeOnly ? 'No older source on record — the trail starts in English.' : 'Its route into English:'}</span>
      <ol aria-label="Route into English" className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-1.5 gap-y-2">
        {stops.map((stop, i) => {
          const isEnglish = i === stops.length - 1;
          const tone = isEnglish
            ? 'bg-accent font-semibold text-white'
            : stop.uncertain
              ? 'border border-dashed border-lock text-muted'
              : 'bg-chip text-ink';
          return (
            <li key={`${stop.lang}-${i}`} className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
              {i > 0 && <ChevronIcon className="size-3 shrink-0 text-faint" />}
              <span className={`${CHIP} ${tone}`}>
                <LanguageName lang={stop.lang} />
                {stop.uncertain && <span className="sr-only"> (uncertain)</span>}
              </span>
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ol>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```typescript
import { Fragment } from 'react';
import type { Clue, WordPart } from '../types';
import { JourneyTrail } from './JourneyTrail';
import { LanguageName } from './LanguageName';
import { RootForm } from './RootForm';

function article(lang: string): string {
  return lang !== 'PIE' && /^[aeiou]/i.test(lang) ? 'an' : 'a';
}

const quote = (gloss: string) => `‘${gloss}’`;

function PartsList({ parts, showForms }: { parts: WordPart[]; showForms: boolean }) {
  if (!showForms) {
    return <>Built from parts meaning {parts.map((p) => quote(p.gloss ?? '')).join(' + ')}.</>;
  }
  const sharedLang = parts.every((p) => p.lang && p.lang === parts[0].lang) ? parts[0].lang : undefined;
  return (
    <>
      Built from {sharedLang && <><LanguageName lang={sharedLang} /> </>}
      {parts.map((part, i) => (
        <Fragment key={i}>
          {i > 0 && ' + '}
          {!sharedLang && part.lang && <><LanguageName lang={part.lang} /> </>}
          <RootForm>{part.form}</RootForm>
          {part.gloss && ` ${quote(part.gloss)}`}
        </Fragment>
      ))}
      .
    </>
  );
}

export function ClueContent({ clue }: { clue: Clue }) {
  switch (clue.kind) {
    case 'text':
      return <>{clue.text}</>;
    case 'journey':
      return <JourneyTrail stops={clue.stops} />;
    case 'meaning':
      return (
        <>
          {clue.uncertain ? 'May trace back' : 'Traces back'} to {article(clue.lang)} <LanguageName lang={clue.lang} />{' '}
          {clue.lang === 'PIE' ? 'root' : 'word'} meaning {quote(clue.gloss)}.
        </>
      );
    case 'parts':
      return <PartsList parts={clue.parts} showForms={clue.showForms} />;
    case 'source':
      return (
        <>
          {clue.sameSpelling ? 'Same spelling in ' : clue.uncertain ? 'Perhaps from ' : 'From '}
          <LanguageName lang={clue.lang} />
          {clue.sameSpelling ? ': ' : ' '}
          <RootForm>{clue.form}</RootForm>
          {clue.gloss && `, ${quote(clue.gloss)}`}.
        </>
      );
  }
}
```

```typescript
interface LetterHintProps {

/** Always-visible word shape: one dash per letter, plus the count and part of speech. */

      </div>
      <p className="text-[12px] text-muted">
        {count} letters{posLabel && ` · ${posLabel}`}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```typescript
import type { WordEntry } from '../types';
import { formatAttested } from '../lib/puzzle';
import { LanguageName } from './LanguageName';

interface TimelineNodeProps {
  lang: string;
  form?: string;
  gloss?: string;
  meta?: string;
  uncertain?: boolean;
  current?: boolean;
}

function TimelineNode({ lang, form, gloss, meta, uncertain, current }: TimelineNodeProps) {
  return (
    <li className="relative flex flex-col gap-0.5 pl-6">
      <span
        aria-hidden="true"
        className={`absolute top-[2px] left-0 size-2.5 rounded-full ${
          current ? 'bg-accent' : 'border-[1.5px] border-lock bg-card'
        }`}
      />
      <span className="text-[11px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-muted">
        <LanguageName lang={lang} />
        {uncertain && ' · perhaps'}
        {meta && ` · ${meta}`}
      </span>
      {form && <span className="font-serif text-[18px] italic leading-tight text-ink">{form}</span>}
      {gloss && <span className="text-[14px] leading-snug text-muted">‘{gloss.replace(/\.$/, '')}’</span>}
    </li>
  );
}

/** The word's ancestry, oldest first, ending with its arrival in English. */
export function LineageTimeline({ entry }: { entry: WordEntry }) {
  const lineage = entry.roots?.lineage ?? [];
  const attested = entry.roots?.attested;

  return (
    <ol className="relative flex flex-col gap-4 before:absolute before:top-2 before:bottom-2 before:left-[4px] before:w-[1.5px] before:bg-lock">
      {lineage.map((stage, i) => (
        <TimelineNode key={i} lang={stage.lang} form={stage.form} gloss={stage.gloss} uncertain={stage.uncertain} />
      ))}
      <TimelineNode
        lang="English"
        form={entry.word}
        gloss={entry.clues[0]}
        meta={attested ? formatAttested(attested).label : undefined}
        current
      />
    </ol>
  );
}
```

```mjs
// Runs the app's real clue builder over every word in headless Chrome and checks for answer leaks.
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const SCRATCH = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname).replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1');
const PROFILE = path.join(SCRATCH, 'profile-leak');
const CHROME = path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA, 'ms-playwright', 'chromium-1217', 'chrome-win64', 'chrome.exe');
const PORT = 9335;
rmSync(PROFILE, { recursive: true, force: true });
const chrome = spawn(CHROME, ['--headless=new', `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`, `--user-data-dir=${PROFILE}`, '--no-first-run', 'about:blank'], { stdio: 'ignore' });
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
let targets;
for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) { try { targets = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json(); break; } catch { await sleep(200); } }
const ws = new WebSocket(targets.find((t) => t.type === 'page').webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((r) => ws.addEventListener('open', r));
let id = 0; const pending = new Map();
ws.addEventListener('message', (ev) => { const m = JSON.parse(ev.data); if (m.id) pending.get(m.id)?.(m); });
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((res) => { const n = ++id; pending.set(n, (m) => res(m.result ?? m.error)); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: n, method, params })); });
await send('Page.navigate', { url: 'http://localhost:5199/' });
await sleep(2000);

const expression = `(async () => {
  const { WORDS } = await import('/src/lib/puzzle.ts');
  const { getClues } = await import('/src/lib/clues.ts');
  const letters = (s) => s.normalize('NFD').replace(/[\\u0300-\\u036f]/g, '').toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z]/g, '');
  const toText = (c) => {
    switch (c.kind) {
      case 'text': return c.text;
      case 'journey': return c.stops.map((s) => s.lang + (s.uncertain ? '?' : '')).join(' > ');
      case 'meaning': return (c.uncertain ? '[maybe] ' : '') + c.lang + ' meaning "' + c.gloss + '"';
      case 'parts': return c.parts.map((p) => (c.showForms ? (p.lang ? p.lang + ' ' : '') + '<' + p.form + '> ' : '') + (p.gloss ? '"' + p.gloss + '"' : '')).join(' + ');
      case 'source': return (c.sameSpelling ? 'SAME SPELLING in ' : c.uncertain ? 'Perhaps from ' : 'From ') + c.lang + ' <' + c.form + '>' + (c.gloss ? ' "' + c.gloss + '"' : '');
    }
  };
  const problems = []; const dump = []; let masked = 0; const kinds = {};
  for (const e of WORDS) {
    const clues = getClues(e);
    if (clues.length !== 5) problems.push(e.word + ': ' + clues.length + ' clues');
    const answerRe = new RegExp('\\\\b' + e.word + '\\\\b', 'i');
    const forms = [...(e.roots?.lineage ?? []), ...(e.roots?.parts ?? [])].map((s) => s.form).filter((f) => f && letters(f).length >= 4);
    const texts = clues.map(toText);
    texts.forEach((t, i) => {
      if (answerRe.test(t)) problems.push(e.word + ' clue ' + (i + 1) + ' contains the answer: ' + t);
      if (i < 4) for (const f of forms) if (t.includes('<' + f + '>') || new RegExp('(^|[^a-z])' + f.replace(/[.*+?^\${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&') + '([^a-z]|$)', 'i').test(t)) problems.push(e.word + ' clue ' + (i + 1) + ' shows root form ' + f + ': ' + t);
    });
    if (texts[4].includes('\\u00b7')) masked++;
    kinds[clues[4].kind] = (kinds[clues[4].kind] || 0) + 1;
    dump.push('## ' + e.word + '\\n' + texts.map((t, i) => '  ' + (i + 1) + '. ' + t).join('\\n'));
  }
  return { count: WORDS.length, problems, masked, kinds, dump: dump.join('\\n') };
})()`;
const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true });
if (r.exceptionDetails) { console.log('EXCEPTION', r.exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? r.exceptionDetails.text); }
else {
  const v = r.result.value;
  writeFileSync(path.join(SCRATCH, 'clues-dump.txt'), v.dump);
  console.log('words:', v.count, '| clue-5 kinds:', JSON.stringify(v.kinds), '| clue-5 masked:', v.masked);
  console.log('problems:', v.problems.length); v.problems.forEach((p) => console.log('  ' + p));
}
ws.close(); chrome.kill();
```

```mjs
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-26 18:33:33Z)**_

The clues are now about etymology, and the result screen shows each word's history as a timeline. Build and lint pass. I ran the clue builder over all 98 words and no clue contains its answer. I also played several words through in a browser at desktop and phone width with no errors.

**The data:** each word in [words.json](src/words.json) now has a `roots` field with its language chain, word parts and first-recorded date. A script checked all 620+ values: each one appears word for word in that entry's own etymology text, so nothing is invented. Links the text only hedges ("perhaps from…") are marked uncertain and shown that way, with dashed chips and "May trace back to…". The other fields are unchanged.

**The clues**, hardest to easiest, using auspex as the example:
1. The route into English as chips: PIE → Latin → English
2. "First recorded in English in the 1590s." Old dates like "late 14c." are rewritten as "the late 1300s".
3. "Built from parts meaning 'bird' + 'to see'", with meanings only.
4. The earliest English sense, from the original clue data.
5. "Built from PIE \*awi- 'bird' + \*spek- 'to see'", the actual root words.

The letter count is now always visible as a row of dashes with "6 letters · noun" above the guess box.

**Hiding the answer:** root words appear only in clue 5.
- A root that's close to the answer is shown on purpose. Getting from Latin *acerbus* to "acerbic" is the fun part.
- A root spelled the same as the answer is hidden: "Same spelling in Spanish: *b·····*, 'district, suburb'".
- English compounds hide their stems but keep suffixes: backfire shows *b··· + f···*, economical shows *e······· + -al*.

**Result screen:** a "Word history" timeline from the oldest ancestor down to English, the word-part breakdown, and the full etymology collapsed under "Read the full etymology".

**Things you might want to look at:**
- **Final clues that mostly hide the root (31 words).** When the only root spells the answer, clue 5 ends up masked, e.g. cardinal gets "From Latin *c·········*".
- **Clue 3 still uses old stored text for about 16 words.** These are words formed inside English (bangs, firing, haggle), where the etymology gives no older meaning. For them, clue 5 now says "Related to the English word *b···*".
- **galoot:** its origin is officially unknown, so I used the source the dictionary proposes (Spanish *galeoto* "galley slave"), marked uncertain.
- **Compound definitions mention their parts.** The definitions for backfire, backlog, catchword and earthwork contain their own parts ("A fire deliberately lit…"). That's in the original data, so I left it.

The root logic is in [clues.ts](src/lib/clues.ts). The new pieces are [JourneyTrail](src/components/JourneyTrail.tsx), [LineageTimeline](src/components/LineageTimeline.tsx), [LetterHint](src/components/LetterHint.tsx) and [ClueContent](src/components/ClueContent.tsx). Nothing is committed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-26 19:18:32Z)**_

The data comes from two sources.

**The etymology text** (`etymology`, `crossreferences`, `years`, `clues`) was already in [words.json](src/words.json) when I started. I didn't fetch or add any outside data. It looks like it comes from the Online Etymology Dictionary (etymonline.com, by Douglas Harper):
- `App.tsx` originally imported a package called `etymonline`.
- The text is in Etymonline's style: "from PIE root…", "(see acerbity)", citations like "[Watkins]" and "[Century Dictionary]".

The 5 original clues were already in the file too, probably from a script of yours or a teammate's. That script isn't in the repo, so I can't say exactly how they were generated.

**The new `roots` data** is what I extracted by hand in this session, from each entry's own `etymology` text. A script checked that every form, meaning, date and language name appears word for word in that entry's text. There are three caveats:

1. **Some language labels are my inference.** The check only confirms a language name appears somewhere in the text, not that it's attached to that particular form. Where the text chains forms without repeating the language, I carried it over from the previous step:

```bash
const POS = { n: 'noun', v: 'verb', adj: 'adjective', adv: 'adverb' };
const out = (cat, msg) => console.log(`[${cat}] ${msg}`);

// Structure / duplicates
const seen = new Map();
d.forEach((e, i) => {
  if (seen.has(e.word)) out('dup-word', `${e.word} at ${seen.get(e.word)} and ${i}`);
  seen.set(e.word, i);
  if (e.word !== e.word.trim() || /[A-Z]/.test(e.word)) out('word', `odd word "${e.word}"`);
  const keys = Object.keys(e).join(',');
  if (keys !== 'word,pos,crossreferences,etymology,years,clues,roots') out('keys', `${e.word}: ${keys}`);
  if (!Array.isArray(e.clues) || e.clues.length !== 5) out('clues', `${e.word}: ${e.clues?.length}`);
  const dupX = e.crossreferences.filter((x, j, a) => a.indexOf(x) !== j);
  if (dupX.length) out('xref-dup', `${e.word}: ${JSON.stringify(e.crossreferences)}`);
});

// Alphabetical order
d.forEach((e, i) => { if (i && d[i - 1].word.localeCompare(e.word) > 0) out('order', `${d[i - 1].word} before ${e.word}`); });

// Letter-count clue vs word and pos
d.forEach((e) => {
  const c = e.clues[4];
  const m = c.match(/^(\d+) letters, (\w+)$/);
  if (!m) { out('letters-format', `${e.word}: ${c}`); return; }
  if (+m[1] !== e.word.length) out('letters-count', `${e.word} has ${e.word.length} letters but clue says ${m[1]}`);
  const want = POS[e.pos] ?? '(null pos)';
  if (m[2] !== want) out('letters-pos', `${e.word}: pos=${e.pos} but clue says "${m[2]}"`);
});

// years field vs 4-digit years in etymology
d.forEach((e) => {
  const inText = [...new Set((e.etymology.match(/(?<!\d)\d{4}(?!\d)/g) || []).map(Number))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  const ys = [...e.years].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  if (JSON.stringify(inText) !== JSON.stringify(ys)) out('years', `${e.word}: years=${JSON.stringify(e.years)} text has ${JSON.stringify(inText)}`);
});

// Formatting in etymology text
d.forEach((e) => {
  const t = e.etymology;
  if (/\r/.test(t)) out('fmt-CR', `${e.word}: contains \\r`);
  if (/  /.test(t.replace(/\r?\n/g, ''))) out('fmt-2space', `${e.word}: "${t.match(/.{0,25}  .{0,25}/)[0]}"`);
  if (/^\s|\s$/.test(t)) out('fmt-trim', `${e.word}: leading/trailing whitespace`);
  const q = (t.match(/"/g) || []).length; if (q % 2) out('fmt-quotes', `${e.word}: odd number of " (${q})`);
  const o = (t.match(/\(/g) || []).length, c = (t.match(/\)/g) || []).length; if (o !== c) out('fmt-parens', `${e.word}: ( ${o} vs ) ${c}`);
  const bo = (t.match(/\[/g) || []).length, bc = (t.match(/\]/g) || []).length; if (bo !== bc) out('fmt-brackets', `${e.word}: [ ${bo} vs ] ${bc}`);
  if (/\["|"\]/.test(t)) out('fmt-bracket-quote', `${e.word}: "${t.match(/.{0,30}(\["|"\]).{0,5}/)[0]}"`);
});

// Clue text formatting
d.forEach((e) => e.clues.slice(0, 4).forEach((c, i) => {
  if (!/[.!?)'"’]$/.test(c)) out('clue-end', `${e.word} clue ${i + 1}: ${c}`);
  if (/^[a-z]/.test(c)) out('clue-lowercase', `${e.word} clue ${i + 1}: ${c}`);
  if (/[,:;]\.$|\.\.$/.test(c)) out('clue-punct', `${e.word} clue ${i + 1}: ${c}`);
  if (/…$/.test(c)) out('clue-truncated', `${e.word} clue ${i + 1}: ${c.slice(-40)}`);
}));
EOF
```

```cjs
const log = [];

function set(word, path, from, to) {
  const e = byWord[word];
  if (!e) throw new Error('no word ' + word);
  const keys = path.split('.');
  let obj = e;
  for (const k of keys.slice(0, -1)) obj = obj[k];
  const last = keys.at(-1);
  if (from !== undefined && JSON.stringify(obj[last]) !== JSON.stringify(from)) {
    throw new Error(`${word}.${path}: expected ${JSON.stringify(from)} but found ${JSON.stringify(obj[last])}`);
  }
  obj[last] = to;
  log.push(`${word}.${path}`);
}
function replaceIn(word, from, to) {
  const e = byWord[word];
  if (!e.etymology.includes(from)) throw new Error(`${word}: etymology lacks ${JSON.stringify(from)}`);
  e.etymology = e.etymology.replace(from, to);
  log.push(`${word}.etymology`);
}
```

```bash
const d = require('./src/words.json');
const POS = { n: 'noun', v: 'verb', adj: 'adjective', adv: 'adverb', interj: 'interjection' };
const issues = [];
const ws = (s) => s.replace(/[ ]+/g, ' ');
let facts = 0;
for (const e of d) {
  const t = e.etymology;
  if (/\r/.test(t) || /  /.test(t)) issues.push(`${e.word}: whitespace`);
  if ((t.match(/"/g) || []).length % 2) issues.push(`${e.word}: odd quotes`);
  if ((t.match(/\(/g) || []).length !== (t.match(/\)/g) || []).length) issues.push(`${e.word}: parens`);
  if (/\["|"\]/.test(t)) issues.push(`${e.word}: bracket-quote`);
  if (new Set(e.crossreferences).size !== e.crossreferences.length) issues.push(`${e.word}: dup xref`);
  const m = e.clues[4].match(/^(\d+) letters, (\w+)$/);
  if (!m || +m[1] !== e.word.length || m[2] !== POS[e.pos]) issues.push(`${e.word}: letters clue "${e.clues[4]}"`);
  const want = e.roots.attested ? `First attested: ${e.roots.attested}.` : 'No firm early date survives in the record.';
  if (e.clues[1] !== want) issues.push(`${e.word}: date clue`);
  if (/trail runs back|Rooted in God|Phillies Blunt\.$/.test(e.clues.join(' '))) issues.push(`${e.word}: stale clue`);
  const check = (v) => { if (v == null) return; facts++; if (!ws(t).includes(ws(v))) issues.push(`${e.word}: not in text -> ${v}`); };
  check(e.roots.attested);
  for (const s of [...e.roots.lineage, ...e.roots.parts]) { check(s.lang); check(s.form); check(s.gloss); }
}
console.log('entries:', d.length, '| root facts verified verbatim:', facts, '| remaining issues:', issues.length);
issues.forEach((i) => console.log('  ' + i));
EOF
npx tsc -b && npm run lint 2>&1 | tail -1
```

I scanned all 98 words and made 128 fixes in [words.json](src/words.json). Every check passes afterwards:
- The formatting scan and the part-of-speech/letter-count checks find nothing.
- All 625 root facts still appear word for word in their source text.
- The build and lint pass.
- In a browser run over every word, clues 1–4 never contain the answer, part of it, or its stem.

**Wrong facts in the old clues:**
- **Origin clues:** 18 were wrong. goblin claimed to be related to *cobalt*, but the text says "said to be unrelated". goose claimed *tooth*, dream claimed *somnolence*, and bless listed *immolate*, all of which the text only compares. enthusiast said "Rooted in God." Ten words formed in English claimed "Its trail runs back through several older languages".
- **Date clues:** 69 of 98 were fragments or had the wrong year. glucose said "around 1811", the coiner's birth year. goose said 1845, the date of "cook one's goose". gnarl said 1590 and equestrian 1550, both of which belong to different words. All now use the checked first-attested date. The game wasn't showing these, but the file is now consistent.
- **Definitions:** 5 were broken. grenadier's was the fragment "Who were dexterous in flinging…". For aikido and banzai the stored "definition" was the literal Japanese translation. catcall's was just a quote from Samuel Johnson.
- **Secondary-sense clues:** 14 were weak or wrong. Some gave the answer away ("that which is **engraved**", "political **economy**"). bangs' was the meaning of a different phrase. galoot's was just "Dictionary of American Slang." Some added details the text doesn't support, like the "broad-cut" cigars in blunt's.

**Source text:**
- *elementem* is now *elementum*, in both the text and the root data.
- I fixed a missing parenthesis in dream and a broken citation in electrum.
- I normalized Windows line breaks (11 entries) and double spaces (5 entries).

**Structure:**
- backlog had a duplicated cross-reference.
- banzai had no part of speech, which made its letter clue say "word". I set it to interjection, since the text calls it a war-cry. That's a judgment call.

**Code change:** the game now also masks words in clues 1–4 that share a stem with the answer or appear inside it. For example, chieftain's clue 4 becomes "Ruler, c····, head", and backfire's becomes "A f··· deliberately lit…". Before, the definitions of compound words mentioned their own parts.

**Left alone:** I only fixed errors I could confirm. I have no copy of the original Etymonline entries to compare against, so a mistake in the source text that I couldn't recognise myself is still in there.

A backup of the file from before these fixes is at `scratchpad/words.backup.json`. Nothing is committed.

```text
5	  MAX_GUESSES,
6	  WORDS,
7	  getDailyIndex,
8	  getRandomIndex,
9	  isCorrect,
10	  normalizeGuess,
11	  todayKey,
12	} from '../lib/puzzle';
13	import { loadDaily, saveDaily } from '../lib/storage';
14	
15	interface GameState {
16	  mode: GameMode;
17	  /** The calendar day this daily game belongs to; used as its storage key. */
18	  dayKey: string;
19	  wordIndex: number;
20	  wrongGuesses: string[];
21	  status: GameStatus;
22	}
23	
24	function createDailyState(): GameState {
25	  const dayKey = todayKey();
26	  const saved = loadDaily(dayKey);
27	  return {
28	    mode: 'daily',
29	    dayKey,
30	    wordIndex: getDailyIndex(),
31	    wrongGuesses: saved?.wrongGuesses ?? [],
32	    status: saved?.status ?? 'playing',
33	  };
34	}

36	export function useGame() {
37	  const [state, setState] = useState<GameState>(createDailyState);
38	
39	  const entry = WORDS[state.wordIndex];
40	  const clues = getClues(entry);
41	  const wrongCount = state.wrongGuesses.length;
42	  const playing = state.status === 'playing';
43	
44	  function update(next: GameState) {
45	    setState(next);
46	    if (next.mode === 'daily') {
47	      saveDaily(next.dayKey, { wrongGuesses: next.wrongGuesses, status: next.status });
48	    }
49	  }
50	
51	  function submitGuess(raw: string): GuessResult {
52	    const guess = normalizeGuess(raw);
53	    if (!guess || !playing) return 'invalid';
54	    if (state.wrongGuesses.includes(guess)) return 'duplicate';
55	
56	    if (isCorrect(guess, entry)) {
57	      update({ ...state, status: 'won' });
58	      return 'correct';
59	    }
60	
61	    const wrongGuesses = [...state.wrongGuesses, guess];
62	    update({
63	      ...state,
64	      wrongGuesses,
65	      status: wrongGuesses.length >= MAX_GUESSES ? 'lost' : 'playing',
66	    });
67	    return 'wrong';
68	  }
69	
70	  function startPractice() {
71	    setState({
72	      mode: 'practice',
73	      dayKey: todayKey(),
74	      wordIndex: getRandomIndex([getDailyIndex(), state.wordIndex]),
75	      wrongGuesses: [],
76	      status: 'playing',
77	    });
78	  }
79	
80	  function backToDaily() {
81	    setState(createDailyState());
82	  }
83	
84	  return {
85	    mode: state.mode,
86	    status: state.status,
87	    entry,
88	    clues,
89	    wrongGuesses: state.wrongGuesses,
90	    guessesUsed: wrongCount + (state.status === 'won' ? 1 : 0),
91	    guessNumber: Math.min(wrongCount + 1, MAX_GUESSES),
92	    revealedCount: playing ? Math.min(wrongCount + 1, clues.length) : clues.length,
93	    submitGuess,
94	    startPractice,
95	    backToDaily,
96	  };
97	}
```

```typescript
import { useId, useRef, useState, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import type { GuessResult } from '../types';
import { Button } from './Button';

interface GuessFormProps {
  onGuess: (raw: string) => GuessResult;
  onSkip: () => void;
}

export function GuessForm({ onGuess, onSkip }: GuessFormProps) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('');
  const [hint, setHint] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const inputId = useId();
  const hintId = useId();
  const isEmpty = value.trim() === '';

  // Enter on an empty input lands here and is ignored, so a stray Enter never skips.
  function handleSubmit(e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    const result = onGuess(value);
    if (result === 'invalid') return;
    if (result === 'duplicate') {
      setHint('Already guessed — try another word.');
      return;
    }
    setValue('');
    setHint(null);
  }

  function handleSkip() {
    onSkip();
    setHint(null);
    inputRef.current?.focus();
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <div className="flex items-end gap-4">
        <label htmlFor={inputId} className="sr-only">
          Type your guess
        </label>
        <input
          ref={inputRef}
          id={inputId}
          name="guess"
          type="text"
          autoComplete="off"
          autoCapitalize="off"
          spellCheck={false}
          autoFocus
          placeholder="Type your guess…"
          value={value}
          onChange={(e) => {
            setValue(e.target.value);
            setHint(null);
          }}
          aria-describedby={hint ? hintId : undefined}
          className="min-w-0 flex-1 border-0 border-b-[1.5px] border-underline bg-transparent px-1 py-3 text-[17px] text-ink placeholder:text-faint focus:border-accent focus:outline-none"
        />
        {isEmpty ? (
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={handleSkip} className="min-w-24">
            Skip
          </Button>
        ) : (
          <Button type="submit" className="min-w-24">
            Guess
          </Button>
        )}
      </div>
      {hint && (
        <p id={hintId} role="status" className="px-1 text-[13px] italic text-muted">
          {hint}
        </p>
      )}
    </form>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import { SKIPPED } from '../lib/puzzle';
import { XIcon } from './icons';

export function GuessChip({ word }: { word: string }) {
  if (word === SKIPPED) {
    // py-[5px] + 1px border keeps the same height as a guess chip.
    return (
      <li className="inline-flex items-center rounded-[20px] border border-dashed border-lock px-3 py-[5px] text-[13px] italic text-muted">
        Skipped
      </li>
    );
  }
  return (
    <li className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-[20px] bg-chip px-3 py-1.5 text-[13px] uppercase text-muted line-through">
      {word}
      <XIcon className="size-[11px] shrink-0 text-accent" />
    </li>
  );
}
```

```mjs
mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });

const evaluate = async (expression) => { const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true }); if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(r.exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? r.exceptionDetails.text); return r.result.value; };
await send('Page.enable'); await send('Runtime.enable');
```

```typescript
import { useEffect, useState, type CSSProperties } from 'react';

// Parchment accent plus warm companions; ink adds a few dark flecks.
const COLORS = ['var(--color-accent)', '#d08a4e', '#c9a04a', '#5b7b6e', '#8a6e4b', 'var(--color-ink)'];
const PIECE_COUNT = 90;
// Longest delay (0.6s) + longest fall (4.2s), with a little slack.
const LIFETIME_MS = 5000;

interface Piece {
  left: number;
  delay: number;
  duration: number;
  drift: number;
  spin: number;
  flutter: number;
  color: string;
  width: number;
  height: number;
  round: boolean;
}

function makePieces(): Piece[] {
  return Array.from({ length: PIECE_COUNT }, () => {
    const round = Math.random() < 0.25;
    const width = 6 + Math.random() * 6;
    return {
      left: Math.random() * 100,
      delay: Math.random() * 0.6,
      duration: 2.4 + Math.random() * 1.8,
      drift: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 240,
      spin: (Math.random() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * (360 + Math.random() * 540),
      flutter: 0.5 + Math.random() * 0.8,
      color: COLORS[Math.floor(Math.random() * COLORS.length)],
      width,
      height: round ? width : width * (0.4 + Math.random() * 0.5),
      round,
    };
  });
}

function prefersReducedMotion(): boolean {
  return window.matchMedia?.('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ?? false;
}

/** A one-shot shower of paper confetti over the page; removes itself once it has fallen. */
export function Confetti() {
  const [pieces] = useState(() => (prefersReducedMotion() ? [] : makePieces()));
  const [done, setDone] = useState(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => setDone(true), LIFETIME_MS);
    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, []);

  if (done || pieces.length === 0) return null;

  return (
    <div aria-hidden="true" className="pointer-events-none fixed inset-0 z-50 overflow-hidden motion-reduce:hidden">
      {pieces.map((piece, i) => (
        <span
          key={i}
          className="absolute top-0 animate-confetti-fall"
          style={
            {
              left: `${piece.left}%`,
              animationDelay: `${piece.delay}s`,
              animationDuration: `${piece.duration}s`,
              '--drift': `${piece.drift}px`,
              '--spin': `${piece.spin}deg`,
            } as CSSProperties
          }
        >
          <span
            className={`block animate-confetti-flutter ${piece.round ? 'rounded-full' : 'rounded-[1px]'}`}
            style={{
              width: piece.width,
              height: piece.height,
              backgroundColor: piece.color,
              animationDuration: `${piece.flutter}s`,
            }}
          />
        </span>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

```mjs
import path from 'node:path';

const SCRATCH = path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname).replace(/^\/([A-Za-z]:)/, '$1');
const OUT = path.join(SCRATCH, 'shots4');
const PROFILE = path.join(SCRATCH, 'profile4');
const CHROME = path.join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA, 'ms-playwright', 'chromium-1217', 'chrome-win64', 'chrome.exe');
const PORT = 9338;

mkdirSync(OUT, { recursive: true });

const now = new Date();

const chrome = spawn(CHROME, ['--headless=new', `--remote-debugging-port=${PORT}`, `--user-data-dir=${PROFILE}`, '--no-first-run', '--hide-scrollbars', 'about:blank'], { stdio: 'ignore' });
const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
let targets;
for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) { try { targets = await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/json/list`)).json(); break; } catch { await sleep(200); } }
const ws = new WebSocket(targets.find((t) => t.type === 'page').webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((r) => ws.addEventListener('open', r));
let id = 0; const pending = new Map(); const errors = [];
ws.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {
  const m = JSON.parse(ev.data);
  if (m.id) pending.get(m.id)?.(m);
  else if (m.method === 'Runtime.exceptionThrown') errors.push(m.params.exceptionDetails.exception?.description);
  else if (m.method === 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled' && m.params.type === 'error') errors.push(m.params.args.map((a) => a.value ?? a.description).join(' '));
});
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((res, rej) => { const n = ++id; pending.set(n, (m) => (m.error ? rej(new Error(method + ': ' + m.error.message)) : res(m.result))); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: n, method, params })); });
const evaluate = async (expression) => { const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true }); if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(r.exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? r.exceptionDetails.text); return r.result.value; };
await send('Page.enable'); await send('Runtime.enable');

async function load() {

}
async function fresh() { await load(); await evaluate('localStorage.clear()'); await load(); }
async function guess(text) {

  await send('Input.insertText', { text });
  await evaluate(`document.querySelector('form').requestSubmit()`);

  status: document.querySelector('main p')?.textContent,
})`);
const shot = async (name) => { const r = await send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' }); writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, name + '.png'), Buffer.from(r.data, 'base64')); };

try {

  await guess('origin'); await sleep(150);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-26 22:20:44Z)**_

Winning now sets off confetti and a short celebration. Build and lint pass, and I tested it in the browser (screenshots above). No new dependencies.

**What happens on a correct guess:**
- **Confetti:** about 90 paper pieces in rust, gold, sage, brown and ink fall across the screen for about 5 seconds, then disappear. They don't block clicks.
- **The word pops in:** it scales up with a small overshoot and tilt, and the rust line under it draws in from the left.
- **The result panel slides up, and the word history appears one step at a time,** oldest first.

**When it doesn't play:**
- **A loss** gets the slide-up and the timeline, but no confetti or pop.
- **Reloading an already-solved daily word** doesn't replay the confetti. Each new practice win gets its own.
- **Reduced motion:** if the player's system is set to reduce motion, none of the animations run.

**Files:** the confetti is in [Confetti.tsx](src/components/Confetti.tsx), and the animation timings are in [index.css](src/index.css). The other changes are in [useGame.ts](src/hooks/useGame.ts) (a "just won" flag), [ResultPanel.tsx](src/components/ResultPanel.tsx), [LineageTimeline.tsx](src/components/LineageTimeline.tsx) and [App.tsx](src/App.tsx). Nothing is committed.

```typescript
import type { Clue } from '../types';
import { ClueBadge } from './ClueBadge';
import { ClueContent } from './ClueContent';
import { LockIcon } from './icons';

interface ClueRowProps {
  number: number;
  clue: Clue;
  revealed: boolean;
  /** Delay before the unlock animation, in ms. */
  delay?: number;
}

export function ClueRow({ number, clue, revealed, delay = 0 }: ClueRowProps) {
  return (
    <li className="flex items-start gap-3.5 py-[7px]">
      <ClueBadge number={number} revealed={revealed} delay={delay} />
      {revealed ? (
        <div
          className="min-w-0 pt-0.5 text-[15px] leading-normal text-ink motion-safe:animate-clue-in"
          style={{ animationDelay: `${delay}ms` }}
        >
          <ClueContent clue={clue} />
        </div>
      ) : (
        <p className="flex items-center gap-1.5 pt-0.5 text-[15px] italic text-muted">
          <LockIcon className="size-[13px] shrink-0" />
          Unlocks after your next guess
        </p>
      )}
    </li>
  );
}

```

```typescript
import { useId } from 'react';
import type { Clue } from '../types';
import { ClueRow } from './ClueRow';

// A clue unlocks just after the guess chip lands; the rest cascade when the game ends.
const REVEAL_DELAY_MS = 120;
const CASCADE_STEP_MS = 110;

interface ClueListProps {
  clues: Clue[];
  revealedCount: number;
  /** Clues earned by guessing; any beyond this were revealed by the game ending. */
  unlockedCount: number;
}

export function ClueList({ clues, revealedCount, unlockedCount }: ClueListProps) {
  const headingId = useId();

  return (
    <section aria-labelledby={headingId} className="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
      <div className="mb-1.5 flex items-baseline justify-between">
        <h2 id={headingId} className="font-serif text-[18px] font-semibold text-ink">
          Clues
        </h2>
        <span className="text-[12px] text-muted">
          {revealedCount} of {clues.length} revealed
        </span>
      </div>
      <ol aria-live="polite" className="flex flex-col gap-0.5">
        {clues.map((clue, i) => (
          <ClueRow
            key={i}
            number={i + 1}
            clue={clue}
            revealed={i < revealedCount}
            delay={REVEAL_DELAY_MS + Math.max(0, i - unlockedCount + 1) * CASCADE_STEP_MS}
          />
        ))}
      </ol>
    </section>
  );
}

```

```mjs
const OUT = path.join(SCRATCH, 'shots5');
const PROFILE = path.join(SCRATCH, 'profile5');

const ws = new WebSocket(targets.find((t) => t.type === 'page').webSocketDebuggerUrl);
await new Promise((r) => ws.addEventListener('open', r));
let id = 0; const pending = new Map(); const errors = [];
ws.addEventListener('message', (ev) => {
  const m = JSON.parse(ev.data);
  if (m.id) pending.get(m.id)?.(m);
  else if (m.method === 'Runtime.exceptionThrown') errors.push(m.params.exceptionDetails.exception?.description);
  else if (m.method === 'Runtime.consoleAPICalled' && m.params.type === 'error') errors.push(m.params.args.map((a) => a.value ?? a.description).join(' '));
});
const send = (method, params = {}) => new Promise((res, rej) => { const n = ++id; pending.set(n, (m) => (m.error ? rej(new Error(method + ': ' + m.error.message)) : res(m.result))); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: n, method, params })); });
const evaluate = async (expression) => { const r = await send('Runtime.evaluate', { expression, awaitPromise: true, returnByValue: true }); if (r.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(r.exceptionDetails.exception?.description ?? r.exceptionDetails.text); return r.result.value; };
await send('Page.enable'); await send('Runtime.enable');
await send('Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride', { width: 1440, height: 960, deviceScaleFactor: 1, mobile: false });

async function load() {

}
async function fresh() { await load(); await evaluate('localStorage.clear()'); await load(); await sleep(1500); }
async function guess(text) {

  await send('Input.insertText', { text });

}

  const delay = a.effect?.getTiming?.().delay ?? 0;
  return delay ? name + '@' + delay : name;
}).sort()`);
const shot = async (name) => { const r = await send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' }); writeFileSync(path.join(OUT, name + '.png'), Buffer.from(r.data, 'base64')); };

try {

  await fresh();
  await guess('origin');
  await sleep(60);
  console.log('reduced motion   ', JSON.stringify(await active()));
} finally {
  console.log('page errors:', errors.length ? errors : 'none');
  ws.close(); chrome.kill();
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-26 22:28:04Z)**_

The main game now animates throughout. Build and lint pass. I tested it in a headless browser: each event triggers only its own animations, earlier clues and chips don't replay, and the reduced-motion setting turns all movement off. The "failed" notice is from the test server I shut down, not an error.

- **Wrong guess:** the input row shakes, the word pops into Previous guesses, the next dot fills with a little bounce, and "Guess N of 5" ticks up.
- **Repeated guess:** the input row shakes and the "Already guessed" hint slides in, but it doesn't cost a turn.
- **Skip:** the same as a wrong guess, but without the shake.
- **Clue unlock:** the badge pops from its outline state into the filled rust circle, and the clue text slides in from a slight blur. This waits about 0.1s so the chip lands first. When a win reveals the remaining clues, they unlock one after another instead of all at once.
- **Route clue:** its language chips (e.g. PIE → Latin → English) appear one at a time.
- **Page load:** the title and card rise in, and the letter dashes draw in left to right. Each new practice word redraws them.
- **Buttons:** they press down slightly when clicked and fade smoothly on hover.

The timings are all in [index.css](src/index.css) if anything feels too slow or too bouncy. The shake is in [GuessForm.tsx](src/components/GuessForm.tsx) and the clue cascade is in [ClueList.tsx](src/components/ClueList.tsx). Nothing is committed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-26 22:46:32Z)**_

There's no animation library. Everything is plain CSS keyframes wired up through Tailwind, plus one browser API for the shake.

**1. Each animation is defined once in [index.css](src/index.css).** In Tailwind v4, a variable named `--animate-<name>` inside `@theme` becomes a utility class `animate-<name>`:

```css
@theme {
  --animate-chip-in: chip-in 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) both;
  @keyframes chip-in {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.6); }
  }
}
```

Tailwind only includes the keyframes in the build if some component uses that class. The bouncy `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, …)` easing is what gives the pops a slight overshoot. The `both` setting keeps the start state visible during a delay and holds the end state afterwards.

**2. Components add the class with a `motion-safe:` prefix**, e.g. `className="… motion-safe:animate-chip-in"`. The prefix makes it apply only when the player hasn't turned on "reduce motion" in their system settings.

**3. A CSS animation plays when its element first appears on the page, or when the class is added to it.** So most animations need no JavaScript at all:
- **Appearing on the page:** a new guess chip, a newly revealed clue's text, and the result panel animate simply because React adds them to the page.
- **Class added:** a clue badge is the same element before and after it unlocks. When it's revealed, React adds `animate-badge-pop` to its classes, which starts the animation.
- **Forced replay:** giving a React element a `key` that changes makes it re-created, which replays its animation. I used this on the "Guess N of 5" label before you removed its animation.

**4. Staggers are just delays set per element.** The timeline steps, language chips and letter dashes each get an increasing `animationDelay`, e.g. `style={{ animationDelay: `${300 + step * 110}ms` }}`. The end-of-game clue cascade in [ClueList.tsx](src/components/ClueList.tsx) works the same way. Clues you earned by guessing get a fixed 120ms delay. Clues revealed by winning get 110ms more each, so they unlock one after another.

**5. The shake is the exception.** It has to replay on the same input row every wrong guess, and a CSS class can't easily restart. So [GuessForm.tsx](src/components/GuessForm.tsx) uses the browser's built-in animation API directly:

```ts
rowRef.current?.animate(SHAKE, { duration: 380, easing: 'ease-out' });
```

That call can't see the `motion-safe:` prefix, so it checks the setting itself with `prefersReducedMotion()` from [motion.ts](src/lib/motion.ts).

**6. The confetti** ([Confetti.tsx](src/components/Confetti.tsx)) creates 90 pieces once, each with random position, color, size, delay and fall speed. Each piece is two nested elements:
- The outer one falls and spins. Its sideways drift and spin amount come from CSS variables set on that piece, so one set of keyframes gives 90 different paths.
- The inner one runs a looping 3D rotation, so it flips like paper.

The component removes itself after 5 seconds. It only appears when [useGame.ts](src/hooks/useGame.ts) reports a win that happened in this session (`justWon`). That's why reloading a solved game doesn't replay it.
